manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the green orange and place it in the bowl.

Task description: The object is the green orange beside the black mouse, and the target container is the light-blue bowl. Use the currently available right gripper to pick it up and place it.

Success criteria: The green orange is stable in and supported by the light-blue bowl; the gripper is open and has released the fruit.

## Execution tips

- Grip opposite sides of the orange around its wider middle section with the pads, using an opening slightly wider than the grasped area. Leave tabletop clearance for the fingertips to reduce the risk of slipping after gripping near the top or hitting the table.
- Approach through the clearance on the side away from the mouse. Use both views to confirm the fingers enclose the orange before closing, avoiding pushing it into a roll with one finger.
- Use enough grip force to prevent slipping without visibly squeezing the peel. If it slips during a slight lift, let the orange rest on the table again before adjusting the grasp.
- When transporting over a bowl rim, leave height clearance for both the orange bottom and fingertips to pass above it, reducing drops or bowl displacement from contact.
- During placement, leave a gap between the fingers and bowl wall for the fingers to open. Release the orange gently only after it is supported inside the bowl, avoiding gripper contact with the wall or bouncing it out from a height.

After a slight lift, the orange moved up with the gripper, and neither view shows slipping. I will continue lifting to clear the bowl rim, then move toward its center.
The orange remains securely grasped and has been lifted above the bowl rim. I am aligning it over the center of the opening, then will lower in small steps to place it.

A forward-movement request was rejected by the TCP workspace upper x limit, and the arm did not move. I will adjust within the allowed range in this episode, then check whether safe placement inside the bowl is possible.

Within the allowed area, the orange is on the bowl side near the arm. Next I will descend gradually and check clearance between the orange, fingertips, and bowl rim; release only after confirming it is supported inside the bowl.
The orange has been lowered inside the bowl opening, and the bowl has not moved. I am completing the final descent in smaller steps and checking support.

After the gripper opened, the orange fell into the bowl and separated from both fingers. I will move the gripper up slightly, check that the orange remains stable in the bowl, and then end the episode.
